{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Monotone VIs with operator values and a linear-minimization interface.\par}\vspace{5pt}
\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{CV\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}S\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}LMO\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}MONOTONE\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}VI}

Variational inequalities

Solve the monotone VI \AtlasInlineMath{0\in F(z)+N_K(z)}, measuring error by weak gap.

\textbf{Status.} Joint budget unresolved

\textbf{TASK tags.} solution concept: Weak gap; task family: Variational inequality

\textbf{MODEL tags.} monotonicity: Monotone operator; monotonicity: Monotonicity

\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Exact; interface family: Operator and lmo; operation: Linear minimization; operation: Operator value; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared

\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} adaptivity: Adaptive; randomization: Deterministic algorithms

\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required; object: Point; support: Returned atom hull

\textbf{METRIC tags.} criterion: Weak gap

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Solve the monotone VI \AtlasInlineMath{0\in F(z)+N_K(z)}, measuring error by weak gap.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
The set \AtlasInlineMath{K\subset\mathbb{R}^d} is hidden, nonempty, compact, and convex. An enclosing ball, a diameter bound \AtlasInlineMath{D_K}, and a feasible point \AtlasInlineMath{z_0} are public. The operator \AtlasInlineMath{F} is monotone and \AtlasInlineMath{\beta}-Lipschitz on \AtlasInlineMath{K}.

The complete analytic set description is hidden. No extra information sufficient for free projection is supplied.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}

\AtlasMath{z\in K\longmapsto F(z),\qquad c\in\mathbb{R}^d\longmapsto s(c)\in\arg\min_{s\in K}\langle c,s\rangle.}


Both responses are exact. Ties in linear minimization are resolved by an admissible deterministic rule fixed before interaction. Correctness is required for every such rule.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
The output \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{z}} must lie in the convex hull of \AtlasInlineMath{z_0} and all returned \AtlasInlineMath{s(c)}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}

\AtlasMath{G_M(\widehat{z})=\sup_{u\in K}\langle F(u),\widehat{z}-u\rangle.}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
The joint budget is \AtlasInlineMath{(N_F,N_{\rm LMO})}; each operation adds \AtlasInlineMath{1} to its corresponding coordinate. Preserve jointly attainable budgets. Without specified weights, do not sum coordinates or combine coordinatewise bounds from different algorithms.

A fixed joint budget \AtlasInlineMath{(B_F,B_{\rm LMO})} requires \AtlasInlineMath{N_F\le B_F} and \AtlasInlineMath{N_{\rm LMO}\le B_{\rm LMO}} on every admissible instance and every execution path. Early stopping within this budget is allowed.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
Deterministic adaptive algorithms are allowed. Feasible queries and outputs are constructed from the public initial point and returned atoms. Queries outside the unknown set cannot be used to obtain additional information.

The same deterministic algorithm must satisfy the guarantee for every admissible instance.


\AtlasMath{G_M(\widehat{z})\le\varepsilon.}


\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_\allowbreak{}worst\_\allowbreak{}case\_\allowbreak{}cap

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{D_K}: A Euclidean-diameter bound on the feasible domain. \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.

\AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{diam}(K)=\sup_{u,v\in K}\|u-v\|_2\le D_K}

\AtlasInlineMath{\beta}: Euclidean Lipschitz upper bound for the population operator on the declared query domain \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|F(z)-F(w)\|_2\le\beta\|z-w\|_2}

\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Finite Euclidean dimension of the operator domain; regime quantifiers specify whether complexity is uniform in dimension \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Target tolerance for the complete weak-VI gap or global saddle gap, in the units of that gap. \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|\cdot\|_2,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle}: Euclidean norm and inner product; the product-space norm is the square root of the sum of the squared block norms. \textbf{Domain:} The specified finite-dimensional real vector space.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|v\|_2=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}}

\AtlasInlineMath{F}: The unknown operator is single-valued. Monotonicity, strong monotonicity, or weak Minty properties use the specification’s explicit inequalities. \textbf{Domain:} A vector map from the declared query domain into \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{z,u,v}: The operator argument and comparison point in the inequality. \textbf{Domain:} The ambient space is \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^d}. Formulas constrained by \AtlasInlineMath{K} require the corresponding point to lie in \AtlasInlineMath{K}.

\AtlasInlineMath{K}: Hidden nonempty compact convex feasible set; only an enclosing ball, diameter bound, and initial point are public. \textbf{Domain:} A subset of Euclidean space.

\AtlasInlineMath{K\subset\mathbb R^d}

\AtlasInlineMath{N_K(z)}: Use the Euclidean normal cone of the closed convex feasible set K at the feasible point z. The same definition applies blockwise to \AtlasInlineMath{N_X} and \AtlasInlineMath{N_Y}. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{z\in K,\quad N_K(z)\subset\mathbb R^d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{N_K(z)=\{v:\langle v,u-z\rangle\le0\ \forall u\in K\}}

\AtlasInlineMath{z_0,z^\star}: Public initial point and the same solution appearing in the model assumption \textbf{Domain:} Feasible domain of this profile; the distance bound refers to the same solution.

\AtlasInlineMath{\widehat z}: The point or variable blocks ultimately returned by the algorithm, corresponding to the hatted variables in the error formula. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{K\subset\mathbb R^d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{N_F}: The number of complete exact operator-value calls. \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative integer count; expected work is its expectation.

\AtlasInlineMath{N_{\rm LMO}}: Number of linear minimization oracle calls \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative integer count; expected work is its expectation.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal A,I}: An algorithm selected from public inputs and an admissible hidden instance fixed before interaction \textbf{Domain:} The specified algorithm and model classes.

\AtlasInlineMath{c,s(c)}: Linear-objective vector and a minimizer returned by the LMO \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{c\in\mathbb R^d,\ s(c)\in K}.

\AtlasInlineMath{s(c)\in\arg\min_{u\in K}\langle c,u\rangle}

\AtlasInlineMath{G_M}: The weak VI gap at the current feasible point. \textbf{Domain:} A nonnegative real.

\AtlasInlineMath{G_M(z)=\sup_{u\in K}\langle F(u),z-u\rangle}

\AtlasInlineMath{B_F,B_{\rm LMO}}: One algorithm simultaneously meets the fixed operator-value and LMO budgets. \textbf{Domain:} Pair of nonnegative integers.

\needspace{12\baselineskip}\section{3. Complexity bracket}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Compared quantities}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Q1 - achievable resource region}
\AtlasMath{\mathcal B_v(\varepsilon;\theta)=\{b\ge0:\exists\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_v,\ C_j(\mathcal A,I)\le b_j\ \forall j,I,\quad G_v(\mathcal A,I;\varepsilon)\ \forall I\}}
\textbf{Definition.} Jointly attainable budgets under the stated success guarantee

\textbf{Scope.} The full documented joint parameter domain in D\_\allowbreak{}K, beta, d and epsilon, with deterministic Minty-gap guarantee and fixed worst-case two-coordinate budgets. Admitted bounds and their guards are recorded in bounds and comparisons.

\textbf{Optimization direction.} pareto\_\allowbreak{}minimize

Here v is the selected algorithm view, G\_\allowbreak{}v its complete success guarantee, I an admissible fixed instance, theta the remaining parameters, and C\_\allowbreak{}pi the declared resource projection. C\_\allowbreak{}pi uses the view's fixed-path or expected-work budget convention, including initialization. No change of guarantee or scalarization is implicit.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{R1 - The declared parameter domain.}
\textbf{Region.} All admissible parameters in the eight-part specification; subregions with two-sided evidence have not yet been separated.

\textbf{Resource.} Identity projection on the declared joint resource vector; no scalar weights are supplied.

\textbf{Status.} Joint budget unresolved

\textbf{Achievable budgets.} B1, B2, B3

\textbf{Necessary constraints.} B4

\textbf{Gap or comparison.} For epsilon>=beta D\_\allowbreak{}K\textasciicircum{}2, the attainable budget region is exactly \{B\_\allowbreak{}F>=1,B\_\allowbreak{}LMO>=1\}. Otherwise only inner/outer budget-region inclusions are proved; no scalar ratio is defined for this unweighted vector resource. For d=1 the LMO coordinate is exactly 1 with the stated operator allowance. For d>=2 the recorded operator allowance is O(1+R), LMO allowance O((1+R)\textasciicircum{}2), while necessity only gives B\_\allowbreak{}F>=1 and B\_\allowbreak{}LMO>=max(1,[1/(d+1)+8/R]\textasciicircum{}-1-1).

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Write D=\allowbreak{}D\_\allowbreak{}K,\allowbreak{} eta=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}beta,\allowbreak{} C=\allowbreak{}D\textasciicircum{}2,\allowbreak{} delta=\allowbreak{}epsilon/\allowbreak{}(4beta),\allowbreak{} R=\allowbreak{}beta D\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}epsilon. To approximately minimize q(w)=\allowbreak{}eta<g,\allowbreak{}w>+||w-x||\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2 over K,\allowbreak{} initialize s0=\allowbreak{}LMO(g). Since s0 minimizes the linear term,\allowbreak{} H0=\allowbreak{}q(s0)-min q<=\allowbreak{}C/\allowbreak{}2 and its FW gap G0=\allowbreak{}max\_\allowbreak{}v<eta g+s0-x,\allowbreak{}s0-v><=\allowbreak{}C. Thus no bound on ||g|| is required. Quadratic smoothness gives q(s+alpha(v-s))<=\allowbreak{}q(s)-alpha G(s)+C alpha\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2,\allowbreak{} where v=\allowbreak{}LMO(eta g+s-x). If delta>=\allowbreak{}C return s0. Otherwise run m=\allowbreak{}ceil(8C/\allowbreak{}delta) FW updates with alpha\_\allowbreak{}j=\allowbreak{}2/\allowbreak{}(j+2),\allowbreak{} j=\allowbreak{}0,\allowbreak{}...,\allowbreak{}m-1. Convexity gives G>=\allowbreak{}H;\allowbreak{} induction in the preceding descent inequality yields H\_\allowbreak{}m<=\allowbreak{}2C/\allowbreak{}(m+2)<delta/\allowbreak{}4. Now test G using one LMO per test. If G>delta,\allowbreak{} update with alpha=\allowbreak{}delta/\allowbreak{}C. Each failure reduces q by strictly more than delta\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}(2C). Consequently one of n=\allowbreak{}ceil(C/\allowbreak{}(2delta)) tests must succeed,\allowbreak{} since n failures would reduce q by at least delta/\allowbreak{}4,\allowbreak{} contradicting H\_\allowbreak{}m<delta/\allowbreak{}4. Each prox therefore costs at most Q=\allowbreak{}1+ceil(32R)+ceil(2R) LMO calls;\allowbreak{} it uses no new F calls. All updates are convex combinations of already feasible points and returned atoms. Use x1=\allowbreak{}z0;\allowbreak{} for t=\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{}...,\allowbreak{}T=\allowbreak{}ceil(R),\allowbreak{} query F(xt),\allowbreak{} compute yt with this prox at center xt,\allowbreak{} query F(yt),\allowbreak{} and compute x(t+1) with the same center and g=\allowbreak{}F(yt). A successful gap test gives <eta g+w-x,\allowbreak{}w-u><=\allowbreak{}delta for every u in K. The two inequalities,\allowbreak{} the identity for squared distances and eta beta=\allowbreak{}1 give eta<F(yt),\allowbreak{}yt-u><=\allowbreak{}(||xt-u||\textasciicircum{}2-||x(t+1)-u||\textasciicircum{}2)/\allowbreak{}2+2delta:\allowbreak{} the remaining cross term eta<F(yt)-F(xt),\allowbreak{}yt-x(t+1)> is absorbed by (||yt-xt||\textasciicircum{}2+||yt-x(t+1)||\textasciicircum{}2)/\allowbreak{}2. This is also Theorem 3.1 in the read source. Sum over t and use monotonicity <F(u),\allowbreak{}yt-u><=\allowbreak{}<F(yt),\allowbreak{}yt-u>. The average ybar has Minty gap <=\allowbreak{}beta D\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}(2T)+2beta delta<=\allowbreak{}epsilon. Costs on every execution path are at most (2T,\allowbreak{}2TQ),\allowbreak{} including initialization,\allowbreak{} with all F queries and output in the permitted atom hull. Linear minimizers need not be vertices or unique;\allowbreak{} every legal tie choice satisfies the proof.\par\endgroup

For every u in K,\allowbreak{} <F(u),\allowbreak{}s-u>=\allowbreak{}<g,\allowbreak{}s-u>+<F(u)-g,\allowbreak{}s-u><=\allowbreak{}beta||u-z0||||s-u||<=\allowbreak{}beta D\_\allowbreak{}K\textasciicircum{}2,\allowbreak{} because <g,\allowbreak{}s-u><=\allowbreak{}0 by exact linear minimization. This holds for all legal fixed tie choices,\allowbreak{} and output s is an allowed atom. Thus epsilon>=\allowbreak{}beta D\_\allowbreak{}K\textasciicircum{}2 admits budget (1,\allowbreak{}1). Combined with the independently proved necessary B\_\allowbreak{}F,\allowbreak{}B\_\allowbreak{}LMO>=\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{} this determines the entire attainable budget region on this sufficient coarse region. The threshold is an exact sufficient algorithm threshold;\allowbreak{} no assertion of its sharpness is made.\par\endgroup

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy When d=\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{} compact convex K is a closed interval,\allowbreak{} possibly a point,\allowbreak{} and monotonicity means F is nondecreasing. Query F(z0). If it is zero,\allowbreak{} z0 has zero Minty gap. Otherwise call LMO(F(z0));\allowbreak{} the unique relevant endpoint a is the left endpoint when F(z0)>0 and the right endpoint when F(z0)<0. Query F(a). If F(a) has the same weak sign as F(z0),\allowbreak{} output a,\allowbreak{} which solves the VI exactly. Otherwise a and z0 bracket signs. Write the ordered bracket [l,\allowbreak{}r] with F(l)<=\allowbreak{}0<=\allowbreak{}F(r). Repeatedly query its midpoint and retain a sign bracket (stop if the value is zero). After k=\allowbreak{}max(0,\allowbreak{}ceil(log2(beta D\_\allowbreak{}K\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}epsilon)/\allowbreak{}2)) queries the bracket length h<=\allowbreak{}D\_\allowbreak{}K/\allowbreak{}2\textasciicircum{}k. Output its midpoint z. For u outside [l,\allowbreak{}r],\allowbreak{} monotonicity gives F(u)(z-u)<=\allowbreak{}0. Inside,\allowbreak{} the endpoint signs and Lipschitz property give |F(u)|<=\allowbreak{}beta h and |z-u|<=\allowbreak{}h,\allowbreak{} so F(u)(z-u)<=\allowbreak{}beta h\textasciicircum{}2<=\allowbreak{}epsilon. Every queried point and the output is a convex combination of z0 and the sole returned atom. Costs are at most (2+k,\allowbreak{}1),\allowbreak{} including initialization. On epsilon<beta D\_\allowbreak{}K\textasciicircum{}2,\allowbreak{} this dominates the main construction:\allowbreak{} for R>1,\allowbreak{} (log2 R)/\allowbreak{}2<=\allowbreak{}R-1,\allowbreak{} hence k<=\allowbreak{}ceil(R)-1 and 2+k<=\allowbreak{}2ceil(R);\allowbreak{} its LMO allowance is also smaller. On epsilon>=\allowbreak{}beta D\_\allowbreak{}K\textasciicircum{}2 the one-pair upper bound dominates this cap.\par\endgroup
